unit: Ch 5: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Management Assertions in Financial Statements
explain: Assertions are implicit or explicit claims made by management within the financial statements.
The auditor evaluates these claims to identify potential misstatements.
Income statement assertions include Occurrence, Completeness, Cut-off, Accuracy or Measurement, and Presentation and Disclosure.
Balance sheet assertions cover Existence, Completeness, Cut-off, Valuation and Allocation, Rights and Obligations, and Presentation and Disclosure.

flow.title: Auditor's Assertion Verification Path
steps: Management prepares financial statements
Auditor identifies embedded management assertions
Assess risk of material misstatement
Design substantive and control procedures
Gather sufficient appropriate audit evidence

topics.example: If a balance sheet reports Machinery at Rs. 50 lakh, management asserts the machine exists, belongs to the entity, is valued properly, and includes all owned machines.
remember: Income statement checks 'Occurrence' of transactions, while balance sheet checks 'Existence' of balances.
Cut-off ensures transactions are recognized in the correct accounting period.
mistakes: Confusing 'Occurrence' (transactions actually happened) with 'Existence' (assets or liabilities actually exist at date).

quiz.q: Which assertion verifies that recorded revenue transactions genuinely took place and belong to the company?
o: Occurrence
Completeness
Valuation
Existence
quiz.why: Occurrence confirms that recorded transactions in the income statement actually took place and pertain to the entity.

quiz.q: Checking whether goods held on consignment are excluded from the entity's inventory tests which assertion?
o: Cut-off
Rights and Obligations
Accuracy
Measurement
quiz.why: Rights and obligations ensures the entity owns the assets reported and excludes goods belonging to third parties.

topics.title: Audit of Share Capital
explain: Auditor verifies authorized capital against the Memorandum of Association and changes approved via board or general meeting resolutions.
Under Section 53, shares cannot be issued at a discount, except sweat equity (Sec 54) or debt-to-equity conversions under RBI schemes.
Securities premium (Sec 52) can only be applied for specified purposes like bonus shares, preliminary expenses write-off, or buybacks (Sec 68).
Capital reduction under Section 66 requires a special resolution, confirmation by the Tribunal, and filing with the Registrar.
Schedule III requires disclosure of reconciliation of share counts, promoter shareholding, and shareholders holding over 5% shares.

flow.title: Verification of Share Capital
steps: Tally opening balances with prior year
Examine board and shareholder resolutions
Verify compliance with statutory issue provisions
Confirm statutory filings like PAS-3 and SH-7
Examine Schedule III disclosure notes

topics.example: If a company raises fresh equity at Rs. 15 per share (face value Rs. 10), the auditor checks that Rs. 5 per share is credited to the Securities Premium Account.
remember: Section 53 penalizes discounted share issues up to the amount raised or Rs. 5 lakh, whichever is less, plus 12% p.a. refund interest.
Schedule III requires promoter shareholding details and percentage change during the year.
mistakes: Thinking increase in authorized share capital requires a special resolution; an ordinary resolution alters the capital clause of the MOA.

quiz.q: Under Section 53 of the Companies Act, 2013, which shares can legally be issued at a discount to employees?
o: Sweat equity shares
Right shares
Bonus shares
Preference shares
quiz.why: Sweat equity shares issued under Section 54 are a statutory exception to the prohibition on issuing shares at a discount.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT an allowed use of securities premium under Section 52(2)?
o: Issuing unissued shares as bonus shares
Writing off preliminary expenses
Distributing regular cash dividends
Buying back own securities under Section 68
quiz.why: Securities premium is a restrictive capital reserve and cannot be used to pay regular cash dividends.

topics.title: Audit of Reserves and Surplus
explain: Reserves are profits set aside that are not meant to meet any known liability, contingency, or asset diminution.
Revenue reserves are free for distribution to owners, whereas Capital reserves are restricted and cannot be freely distributed.
The auditor traces opening reserves to previous audited accounts and verifies current additions or movements.
Dividends declared after the balance sheet date cannot be booked as a liability as of the balance sheet date under AS 4 / IND AS 10.
A debit balance in the profit and loss account must be shown as a negative figure under 'Surplus' within Reserves and Surplus.

flow.title: Audit Steps for Reserves and Surplus
steps: Match opening balances to audited financials
Vouch profit transfer from profit and loss
Inspect board recommendations and AGM dividend declarations
Verify restrictions on utilization of reserves
Review classification under Schedule III heads

topics.example: If the company creates a Capital Redemption Reserve during preference share redemption, the auditor checks Section 55 compliance ensuring it is only used for bonus shares.
remember: A negative net figure for Reserves and Surplus is still shown under the head 'Reserves and Surplus'.
Earmarked investments representing a reserve must be termed as a 'Fund'.
mistakes: Classifying general reserves as capital reserves; general reserves represent divisible profits and are revenue reserves.

quiz.q: How should a debit balance in the statement of profit and loss be disclosed under Schedule III?
o: As a separate asset under non-current assets
As a negative figure under the head Surplus
Deducted from paid-up share capital directly
Under other current liabilities
quiz.why: Schedule III requires a debit balance in the profit and loss account to be shown as a negative figure under 'Surplus'.

quiz.q: Proposed dividend declared after the balance sheet date but before approval of financials is:
o: Recognized as a current liability
Disclosed in notes without liability recognition
Ignored completely by the auditor
Charged directly to capital reserve
quiz.why: Under AS 4 / IND AS 10, dividends declared after the reporting period are disclosed in notes and not recognized as liabilities at the balance sheet date.

topics.title: Audit of Borrowings
explain: Auditor verifies that borrowings are authorized by board resolutions and within borrowing limits under Section 180.
Direct external balance confirmations (SA 505) must be obtained from banks and lenders for outstanding loans and securities.
The auditor examines loan covenants; non-compliance may necessitate classifying a long-term loan as a current liability.
Current maturities of long-term borrowings must be segregated and disclosed under other current liabilities / short-term borrowings.
Statutory charges must be verified with the Register of Charges and filings with the Registrar of Companies.

flow.title: Audit Procedure for Borrowings
steps: Examine board approvals and borrowing powers
Send external confirmations to all lenders
Recompute interest accruals and loan amortization
Verify creation and registration of charges
Check proper long-term and short-term presentation

topics.example: A company takes an 8-year term loan where Rs. 20 lakh is repayable in the next 12 months. The auditor ensures this Rs. 20 lakh is presented under current maturities.
remember: Any unutilized loan proceeds taken for a specific purpose must be disclosed in notes detailing how they are deployed.
If an entity is declared a wilful defaulter by a bank, the date of declaration and default details must be disclosed.
mistakes: Failing to disclose guarantees given by directors for corporate loans under each relevant loan head as required by Schedule III.

quiz.q: What must an auditor check if the value of security falls below the outstanding bank loan balance?
o: Write off the difference immediately as bad debt
Ensure the loan is classified as secured only up to market value of security
Qualify the audit report automatically
Classify the entire loan as an equity instrument
quiz.why: Loans are classified as secured only to the extent of the market value of the underlying security; the excess becomes unsecured.

quiz.q: Under Schedule III, where should current maturities of long-term debt be presented?
o: Long-Term Borrowings
Other Current Liabilities or Short-Term Borrowings
Non-Current Provisions
Contingent Liabilities
quiz.why: Portions of long-term debt maturing within 12 months must be disclosed separately as current liabilities.

topics.title: Audit of Trade Receivables
explain: Auditor tests internal controls over billing, dispatches, credit approval, and segregation of duties.
Direct confirmations (SA 505) are obtained directly from customers; blank confirmation forms without balance are preferable.
Cut-off testing on sales invoices of the last few days prevents artificial inflation of sales and receivables.
Valuation is tested by reviewing the ageing schedule, identifying disputed or litigated balances, and assessing doubtful debt allowances.
Schedule III mandates an ageing schedule split into undisputed/disputed and considered good/doubtful across defined time buckets.

flow.title: Debtors Verification Sequence
steps: Test internal controls over billing and collections
Obtain trade receivables ageing report
Send external balance confirmations independently
Perform alternative procedures for non-replies
Evaluate adequacy of allowance for doubtful debts

topics.example: For a customer not responding to confirmation, the auditor tests subsequent bank collections and checks original sales contracts and shipping delivery challans.
remember: Ageing buckets for debtors: Less than 6 months, 6 months - 1 year, 1-2 years, 2-3 years, and More than 3 years.
Receivables due by directors or related entities must be separately stated.
mistakes: Permitting client personnel to collect or handle confirmation letters instead of receiving them directly.

quiz.q: Which confirmation request form is generally preferable when auditing trade receivables?
o: Form mentioning the ledger balance to agree
Form without any balance mentioned therein
Oral telephone confirmation
Email copy sent through the client sales team
quiz.why: A blank form without balance is preferable because it forces the debtor to verify and report their own book figures.

quiz.q: Examining shipping records of the last 5 days before year-end against sales invoices primarily validates which assertion?
o: Rights and obligations
Completeness and Cut-off
Presentation
Valuation
quiz.why: Cut-off procedures around year-end ensure that sales and related receivables are recorded in the proper period.

topics.title: Audit of Cash and Cash Equivalents
explain: Cash balances require surprise physical verification in the presence of the cashier to prevent misappropriation.
All cash points (petty cash, main cash, branches) should be counted simultaneously to prevent transfers hiding shortages.
The auditor independently obtains Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS) and verifies uncredited deposits and unpresented cheques.
Cheques unpresented for over 3 months are stale and must be written back to liabilities rather than carried in BRS.
Direct balance confirmation should ideally be sought for 100% of bank accounts.

flow.title: Cash and Bank Verification Process
steps: Conduct surprise simultaneous cash count
Obtain signed count sheet from custodian
Send direct balance confirmation to banks
Examine and test bank reconciliation statements
Verify subsequent period clearances of cheques

topics.example: During a cash count, an I.O.U slip of Rs. 5,000 signed by an employee is found; the auditor verifies authorized approval and ensures it is booked as an advance.
remember: Bank deposits with more than 12 months maturity must be disclosed separately.
Earmarked balances such as unpaid dividend accounts must be separately disclosed.
mistakes: Counting cash in the absence of the cashier, which allows the custodian to dispute any discovered cash shortage.

quiz.q: What should the auditor do regarding cheques issued that have remained unpresented for more than 3 months?
o: Continue showing them in BRS indefinitely
Cancel them and restore the liability in books
Write them off directly to capital reserve
Treat them as an expense item
quiz.why: Stale cheques (over 3 months) become invalid for payment and must be added back to bank balance and recorded as liabilities.

quiz.q: Why must an auditor count multiple cash balances simultaneously across different cashiers?
o: To save audit working hours
To prevent shortages being covered by inter-cash transfers
To comply with Income Tax guidelines
To prepare the petty cash register
quiz.why: Simultaneous verification ensures funds from one till are not quickly transferred to mask a deficit in another.

topics.title: Audit of Inventories
explain: Auditor participates in physical inventory counts to verify existence, observe procedures, and perform test counts.
Cut-off testing involves inspecting the last 5-10 goods receipt notes and dispatch notes around the reporting date.
Under AS 2, inventory is valued at the lower of cost and net realizable value (NRV) on a consistent basis (e.g., FIFO or weighted average).
Inventories held with third parties (e.g., job workers) require independent written confirmations or physical inspection.
Damaged, slow-moving, or obsolete stock must be identified and written down to its estimated net realizable value.

flow.title: Inventory Audit Steps
steps: Review management count instructions and plan
Observe physical count and perform sample test counts
Perform purchase and dispatch cut-off tests
Obtain confirmations for stocks held with third parties
Verify valuation testing lower of cost or NRV

topics.example: Raw materials bought for Rs. 100/kg have a replacement market price of Rs. 70/kg while the finished good sells at a loss; the auditor ensures stock is written down.
remember: Schedule III mandates disclosure of goods-in-transit separately under each inventory sub-category.
Consignment goods held on behalf of others must be excluded from the inventory.
mistakes: Assuming physical counting is the sole responsibility of the auditor; management is responsible for counting while the auditor observes.

quiz.q: Under AS 2, how must an entity value its year-end inventory?
o: At replacement cost only
At net realisable value only
At lower of cost and net realisable value
At historical cost plus standard margin
quiz.why: AS 2 mandates valuation at the lower of cost and net realizable value applied consistently.

quiz.q: How should goods-in-transit be disclosed in company balance sheets according to Schedule III?
o: Under other current assets as an advance
Separately under each respective sub-head of inventory
Aggregated as a single line item under borrowings
Only by way of footnote without amounts
quiz.why: Schedule III requires goods-in-transit to be specified under the relevant sub-heads of inventory like raw materials or finished goods.

topics.title: Audit of Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE)
explain: Costs directly attributable to bringing an asset to its operating location and condition are capitalized.
Testing costs are capitalized after netting off test-sale proceeds, while inaugural and administrative costs must be expensed.
The auditor reconciles physical count reports with the Fixed Asset Register (FAR) and checks that retired assets are deleted.
Ownership is confirmed by inspecting original registered title deeds or obtaining lender confirmations if mortgaged.
Schedule III requires CWIP ageing schedules and specific disclosure if immovable property title deeds are not in the company's name.

flow.title: PPE Audit Procedure
steps: Review physical verification reports against asset register
Verify capital versus revenue classification of additions
Inspect title deeds, conveyance deeds, or lender confirmations
Recalculate depreciation and test for impairment indicators
Check CWIP ageing and Schedule III disclosure notes

topics.example: When auditing a newly acquired factory building, the auditor inspects the registered sale deed and verifies that stamp duty was capitalized as part of the asset cost.
remember: Inauguration costs, advertising expenses, and staff training costs can never be capitalized into PPE.
CWIP ageing requires buckets: Less than 1 year, 1-2 years, 2-3 years, and More than 3 years.
mistakes: Starting depreciation from the date of active commercial production rather than from when the asset is 'available for use'.

quiz.q: Which of the following costs can be capitalized into the cost of a new plant under AS 10 (Revised)?
o: Opening ceremony and inauguration costs
Costs of testing whether the asset functions properly
General administrative overheads
Staff training expenses for operating the plant
quiz.why: Testing costs are directly attributable to bringing the asset to working condition, whereas inauguration and training are expensed.

quiz.q: If title deeds of an immovable property are deposited with a bank as loan security, how does the auditor verify ownership?
o: Obtain written confirmation from the financing bank
Rely entirely on verbal statements of the CEO
Treat the property as non-existent
Wait until the loan is fully repaid
quiz.why: The auditor obtains a direct confirmation from the lending bank that holds the original title deeds as collateral.

topics.title: Audit of Intangible Assets
explain: Intangible assets are non-monetary assets without physical substance, identifiable and controlled for economic benefits.
Internally generated goodwill must never be capitalized in the financial statements under AS 26.
Expenditure on research (or the research phase of an internal project) must always be charged as an expense when incurred.
Development expenditure can only be capitalized if it meets the specific recognition criteria under AS 26.
Schedule III requires disclosure of intangible assets under development ageing schedule in defined time brackets.

flow.title: Audit Steps for Intangible Assets
steps: Assess whether expenditure meets AS 26 recognition criteria
Ensure research expenditure is charged off to profit and loss
Verify purchase contracts and legal ownership documentation
Verify active usage and amortisation calculation
Check disclosures for intangible assets under development

topics.example: A software package purchased to run accounting operations is capitalized as an intangible asset, whereas in-house basic research for new code is expensed immediately.
remember: Computer software that is integral to hardware (like an OS) is treated as PPE, not as a separate intangible asset.
Revaluation changes of 10% or more in the aggregate net carrying value require separate disclosure.
mistakes: Capitalizing research expenses as intangible assets under development.

quiz.q: Under AS 26, how should costs incurred during the research phase of an internal project be treated?
o: Capitalized as Intangible Asset
Recognized as an expense when incurred
Accumulated under Capital Work in Progress
Deferred and amortized over ten years
quiz.why: AS 26 strictly prohibits capitalizing research phase expenditures; they must be expensed immediately.

quiz.q: Which item can never be recognized as an asset in the balance sheet under AS 26?
o: Purchased computer software
Internally generated goodwill
Purchased patent rights
Acquired brand licenses
quiz.why: AS 26 explicitly prohibits the recognition of internally generated goodwill as an asset.

topics.title: Audit of Trade Payables and Other Current Liabilities
explain: Auditor tests purchase controls, goods receipt notes, and the 2-way or 3-way matching process.
External balance confirmation is employed; non-replies are tested via subsequent payments and invoice inspection.
Cut-off testing ensures all goods received before year-end are booked as purchases and creditors.
Unpaid balances to Micro and Small Enterprises must disclose overdue principal, interest paid under Section 16, and interest accrued.
Schedule III mandates trade payables ageing schedules split into MSME and Non-MSME, disputed and undisputed.

flow.title: Trade Payables Audit Sequence
steps: Evaluate purchase ordering and invoice matching controls
Obtain trade payables ledger and ageing schedule
Circularize external balance confirmations
Perform year-end cut-off tests on purchase inward records
Verify MSMED Act disclosures and overdue interest

topics.example: The auditor tests the gate inward register for the last 5 days of March to confirm that all received materials were included in creditors and stock.
remember: Interest payable under the MSMED Act, 2006 is disallowed as a tax deduction under Section 23 of that Act.
Unbilled dues in trade payables must be disclosed separately in the ageing schedule.
mistakes: Failing to review subsequent period payments to uncover unrecorded liabilities existing at the balance sheet date.

quiz.q: Interest paid or payable under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 is:
o: Allowed as tax deductible business expenditure
Disallowed as a deductible expenditure under Section 23
Added directly to the capital reserve account
Exempted from financial statement disclosure
quiz.why: Section 23 of the MSMED Act prohibits allowing such interest as a deductible business expense for income tax.

quiz.q: What is the primary audit purpose of reviewing subsequent expense vouchers after the year-end date?
o: To confirm next year's budget
To detect unrecorded liabilities belonging to the audit period
To evaluate credit ratings of suppliers
To verify statutory filing fee structures
quiz.why: Checking subsequent vouchers reveals expenses that pertained to the year under audit but were omitted from payables.

topics.title: Audit of Loans and Advances and Other Current Assets
explain: Auditor verifies loan agreements, powers under Articles of Association, and board approvals for lending.
External balance confirmations should be circulated for principal amounts plus any accrued interest.
Loans to promoters, directors, and KMPs that are repayable on demand or lack repayment terms require specific disclosure.
Statutory asset balances like GST input tax credit are reconciled with statutory returns filed with the government.
Adequacy of provisions for doubtful loans and advances is scrutinized using an ageing report and litigation history.

flow.title: Audit of Loans and Advances
steps: Examine loan agreements and sanction limits
Confirm board approval in directors' meeting minutes
Circularize direct balance confirmations including interest
Reconcile statutory tax credits with monthly returns
Evaluate recoverability and doubtful advance provisions

topics.example: A company extends a Rs. 10 lakh loan to a director with no specified repayment tenure; the auditor ensures this is disclosed under the promoter/director loans table.
remember: Loans must be classified as secured, unsecured, or doubtful under Schedule III.
Advances to directors or firms where directors are partners must be separately disclosed.
mistakes: Forgetting to calculate and accrue interest on recoverable loans in accordance with the underlying loan agreement.

quiz.q: Which disclosure is specifically required for loans granted to promoters or KMPs under Schedule III?
o: Details of loans that are repayable on demand or without terms
Bank accounts used to transfer the money only
Personal credit scores of the promoters
Net worth certificates of the borrowers
quiz.why: Schedule III requires disclosing the amount and percentage of loans granted to promoters/directors/KMPs that are repayable on demand or have no repayment terms.

quiz.q: How should an auditor verify the validity of GST input tax credit shown under other current assets?
o: Reconcile books with filed statutory GST returns
Take only an oral representation from the tax manager
Ignore balances below Rs. 1 crore
Assume all purchases carry refundable credit
quiz.why: The auditor must tally the input tax ledger in the accounts with the actual statutory tax returns filed with tax authorities.

topics.title: Audit of Provisions and Contingent Liabilities
explain: A provision is recognized when there is a present legal/constructive obligation from a past event, probable outflow, and reliable estimate.
If an outflow is possible or remote, or cannot be measured reliably, it is treated as a contingent liability (or ignored if remote).
When management relies on an actuary or legal expert, the auditor must assess the expert's competence, capability, and objectivity under SA 500.
The auditor must obtain a written management representation confirming that all required provisions have been made.
Schedule III requires classifying provisions into long-term and short-term, separate for employee benefits and others.

flow.title: Evaluating Provisions and Contingencies
steps: Inspect customer contracts and pending legal cases
Test probability criteria of outflow (probable, possible, remote)
Evaluate competence and assumptions of management's expert
Recompute provision calculations and verify movements
Review Schedule III and AS 29 disclosure notes

topics.example: A customer files a Rs. 50 lakh warranty claim; the auditor reviews legal counsel opinions to decide whether to recognize a provision or disclose a contingent liability.
remember: Provisions involve estimation; contingent liabilities are not recognized in the balance sheet but disclosed in notes.
Contingent liabilities with remote possibility of outflow do not require disclosure.
mistakes: Accepting the work of a management expert without evaluating their competence, independence, and underlying data under SA 500.

quiz.q: Under AS 29, a provision is recognized when the outflow of resources embodying economic benefits is:
o: Probable
Possible
Remote
Virtually impossible
quiz.why: A provision is recognized only when the outflow is probable (more likely than not) and reliably estimable.

quiz.q: When evaluating the report of an actuarial expert used by management, the auditor follows which auditing standard?
o: SA 500
SA 210
SA 700
SA 505
quiz.why: SA 500 'Audit Evidence' governs evaluating the competence, capabilities, and objectivity of a management's expert.

topics.title: Additional Regulatory Disclosures & Financial Ratios
explain: Schedule III requires disclosure of 11 key financial ratios for both the current and preceding financial years.
The company must define items included in the numerator and denominator for all disclosed ratios.
Any variance in a ratio exceeding 25% compared to the preceding year requires detailed explanatory commentary.
Companies must disclose details of any Benami property proceedings initiated or pending under the Benami Transactions Act.
Transactions and balances with companies struck off by the Registrar of Companies must be explicitly detailed.

flow.title: Ratio and Regulatory Compliance Check
steps: Compute the 11 mandatory financial ratios
Compare current year ratios with prior year
Identify variances exceeding 25 percent
Obtain management explanations for major variances
Verify disclosures regarding struck off entities and Benami assets

topics.example: If the Debt-Equity ratio changes from 1:1 to 1.5:1 (a 50% jump), the auditor ensures management provides a footnote explaining the fresh borrowings.
remember: Mandatory ratios include Current, Debt-Equity, DSCR, ROE, Inventory Turnover, Debtors Turnover, Creditors Turnover, Net Capital Turnover, Net Profit, ROCE, and ROI.
Variance explanation threshold is strictly more than 25%.
mistakes: Omitting the explanation of numerator and denominator components used to calculate the mandatory ratios.

quiz.q: Under Schedule III, explanation is mandatory if a financial ratio changes as compared to the preceding year by more than:
quiz.why: Schedule III mandates explanatory notes for any change in a ratio by more than 25% compared to the previous year.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the 11 ratios mandatorily disclosed under Schedule III?
o: Current Ratio
Price to Earnings (P/E) Ratio
Debt Service Coverage Ratio
Net Profit Ratio
quiz.why: P/E ratio is a market multiple, not one of the 11 operational and financial ratios mandated by Schedule III.

topics.title: Audit of Revenue from Operations
explain: Revenue risk of material misstatement is presumed high under SA 315; auditors must test both controls and substantive procedures.
Occurrence is tested by vouching sales entries to customer orders, delivery challans, invoices, and bank receipts.
Substantive analytical procedures involve trend comparisons, monthly product-wise sales expectations, and GST reconciliations.
Credit notes issued post year-end must be audited to ensure fictitious sales were not booked to meet targets and reversed later.
Schedule III requires non-finance companies to separately disclose revenue from sale of products, services, other operating revenues, and excise duty.

flow.title: Revenue Verification Process
steps: Understand revenue cycle and test internal controls
Vouch sample sales invoices from inception to collection
Perform sales cut-off tests at year end
Reconcile sales turnover with filed GST returns
Inspect post-year-end credit notes for reversals

topics.example: The auditor tests a sale transaction end-to-end: verifies customer PO, goods dispatch note, GST sales invoice, and bank credit advice.
remember: For finance companies, revenue from operations includes Interest and Other Financial Services.
Trade discounts are deducted from turnover, but unusual discounts and brokerages must be analyzed.
mistakes: Recognizing revenue upon invoice creation rather than when risks and rewards of ownership pass to the customer.

quiz.q: Why does the auditor examine credit notes issued after the close of the financial year?
o: To calculate customer satisfaction indices
To detect window dressing or fictitious year-end sales reversals
To confirm marketing budget utilization
To compute advance income tax liabilities
quiz.why: Post-year-end credit notes often reveal artificial sales booked prior to year-end to meet targets and subsequently cancelled.

quiz.q: Reconciling sales reported in the statement of profit and loss with GST returns verifies primarily which assertions?
o: Completeness and Accuracy
Rights and Obligations
Presentation only
Valuation of equity
quiz.why: GST turnover reconciliations provide evidence that all sales are completely and accurately reported in the accounting records.

topics.title: Audit of Other Income
explain: Other income covers non-core earnings such as bank interest, dividends, and profit/loss on sale of investments.
Interest on fixed deposits is recognized on a time-proportion basis taking into account principal and applicable rates.
Dividends are recognized only when the shareholder's legal right to receive payment is established.
Gain or loss on mutual fund investments is recognized upon transfer of title, measured against carrying values.
Auditor reconciles interest income with Form 26AS (tax credit statement) and direct bank confirmation certificates.

flow.title: Other Income Verification Flow
steps: Obtain schedule of fixed deposits and mutual funds
Recompute interest income on time proportion basis
Match TDS and interest with Form 26AS statements
Verify dividend receipts against dividend declaration notices
Confirm gain or loss on investment sales with fund statements

topics.example: A company holds an FD of Rs. 10 lakh at 7% p.a. for 6 months; the auditor recomputes Rs. 35,000 interest and reconciles it with the bank interest certificate.
remember: Schedule III requires classifying other income into Interest, Dividend, Net gain/loss on sale of investments, and Other non-operating income.
Undisclosed income surrendered in income tax assessments must be disclosed under additional information.
mistakes: Recognizing dividend income when the investee company proposes it, rather than when the right to receive is established.

quiz.q: When should dividend income be recognized in the statement of profit and loss?
o: When the board of the investee recommends it
When the entity's right to receive payment is established
Only upon actual credit into the bank account
At the beginning of the investee's financial year
quiz.why: Dividend income is recognized when the company's right to receive payment is legally established (e.g., declared by shareholders in AGM).

quiz.q: How does an auditor independently verify interest earned on bank fixed deposits?
o: By recomputing interest and reconciling with Form 26AS and bank certificates
By asking the receptionist for verbal confirmation
By checking only the cash book balance
By verifying the company's sales register
quiz.why: Recomputing the interest on a time-proportion basis and cross-checking with Form 26AS and bank statements provides solid audit evidence.

topics.title: Audit of Purchases
explain: Purchases cycle covers requisitioning, ordering, receipt, quality checking, invoice verification, and payment.
Auditor tests 2-way matching (PO and invoice) or 3-way matching (PO, GRN, and vendor invoice).
Inward gate registers and GRNs are checked to confirm physical receipt of goods and prevent fictitious purchases.
Purchase cut-off procedures check the last 5 transactions before year-end to ensure proper accounting period recording.
Analytical procedures include raw material consumption analysis, stock composition analysis, and creditor turnover comparisons.

flow.title: Purchase Audit Procedures
steps: Evaluate purchase authorization and vendor selection
Test 3-way match: PO, GRN, and vendor invoice
Perform cut-off checks on gate inward records
Reconcile input tax ledger with GSTR returns
Perform raw material consumption and analytical tests

topics.example: The auditor selects a purchase invoice of Rs. 4 lakh, verifies the purchase order approval, the warehouse GRN stamp, and the entry in the security gate register.
remember: Purchases from related parties must be checked for board approvals and arm's length pricing.
Schedule III mandates separate disclosure of purchases of stock-in-trade and changes in inventories.
mistakes: Vouching purchase entries against photocopies instead of insisting on original vendor invoices.

quiz.q: What does a 3-way match in the purchase auditing procedure compare?
o: Purchase Order, Goods Receipt Note, and Vendor Invoice
Quotation, Bank Statement, and Sales Order
Cash book, Passbook, and Petty Cash Voucher
Directors Report, Balance Sheet, and P&L
quiz.why: A 3-way match ensures the quantity and price ordered (PO), received (GRN), and billed (Invoice) are completely consistent.

quiz.q: Comparing raw material consumed as a percentage of production with prior years is an example of:
o: Test of details
Substantive analytical procedure
Inquiry only
Reperformance of physical count
quiz.why: Consumption analysis is a substantive analytical procedure used to identify unusual fluctuations in material usage.

topics.title: Audit of Employee Benefits Expenses
explain: Employee benefits include salaries, wages, bonus, PF, ESI, gratuity, leave encashment, and ESOP expenses.
Auditor tests internal controls over biometric attendance, payroll master modifications, and salary approvals.
Risk of fictitious employees is mitigated by surprise personal meetings and verifying employee bank account details.
The auditor carries out analytical tests comparing monthly payroll totals and calculating average salary per employee.
Statutory deductions (PF and ESI) are verified against basic wages and verified using monthly bank deposit challans.

flow.title: Audit Steps for Payroll Expenses
steps: Understand and test attendance and payroll controls
Sample new hires' letters and resigned employees' settlements
Calculate monthly payroll reasonability and trend analysis
Verify PF and ESI computations and deposit challans
Ensure year-end accruals for bonus and gratuity

topics.example: To verify new employee additions, the auditor samples 5 joiners, examines their signed appointment letters, and checks their first month salary credit in the bank statement.
remember: Schedule III requires separate disclosure of salaries & wages, contribution to PF/funds, ESOP/ESPP expenses, and staff welfare.
Full and final settlement sheets of resigned staff must have signed acknowledgements.
mistakes: Overlooking the reconciliation of monthly PF and ESI payment challans with the amounts expensed in the ledger.

quiz.q: Which of the following audit procedures specifically addresses the risk of 'ghost' or fictitious employees?
o: Recomputing monthly depreciation
Meeting employees on a sample basis and testing bank details
Inspecting the fixed assets register
Confirming debtor balances
quiz.why: Verifying identity proofs, bank accounts, and meeting staff in person directly prevents and detects non-existent ghost workers.

quiz.q: Under Schedule III, which employee expense must be disclosed separately from salaries and wages?
o: Expense on ESOP and ESPP
Cost of office stationary
Travelling allowance of auditors
Electricity bill of factory
quiz.why: Schedule III requires separate disclosure of ESOP/ESPP expenses in the notes to employee benefits.

topics.title: Audit of Depreciation and Amortisation
explain: Depreciation allocates the depreciable value of PPE over its useful life; amortisation applies similarly to intangibles.
Depreciation begins strictly when the asset is 'available for use' (in condition and location intended), not when actively operated.
Useful lives must align with Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013, or justifiable technical estimates.
Significant components of an asset with differing useful lives must be depreciated separately (component accounting).
Depreciation changes resulting from revised useful lives or residual values are treated prospectively as changes in accounting estimates.

flow.title: Depreciation Audit Routine
steps: Review entity accounting policy and methods used
Check asset addition dates for 'available for use' timing
Verify useful lives against Schedule II limits
Perform independent recomputation of depreciation expense
Verify Schedule III presentation and accounting disclosures

topics.example: A machine delivered and test-run in April but used in production from October must be depreciated starting from April because it was available for use.
remember: Freehold land is non-depreciable.
Depreciation on revalued amounts must be properly accounted from the revaluation reserve.
mistakes: Deferring depreciation charges until commercial production starts when the asset was already installed and ready months earlier.

quiz.q: When does depreciation of an item of Property, Plant, and Equipment commence?
o: When it is actually put into commercial production
When it is available for use as intended by management
At the end of the financial year automatically
When the purchase invoice is paid in full
quiz.why: Under AS 10, depreciation begins when the asset is in the location and condition necessary for operation (available for use).

quiz.q: Component accounting requires separate depreciation when a component of PPE:
o: Has a cost significant to total cost and a different useful life
Is imported from an overseas supplier
Is painted in a different color
Costs less than Rs. 5,000
quiz.why: AS 10 mandates separate depreciation for every part of an asset that has a significant cost in relation to the total asset cost.

topics.title: Audit of Other Expenses and CSR Disclosures
explain: Other expenses (rent, power, insurance, repairs, legal) are verified for business purpose, authorization, and period cut-off.
Rent is audited by reviewing lease terms, monthly schedules, and straight-lining escalation clauses if applicable.
Insurance policies are audited to segregate prepaid portions from current year expired expenses.
Legal fees are closely scrutinized as they often signal hidden litigation, unrecorded claims, or potential contingent liabilities.
Under Section 135, eligible companies must disclose CSR amount required, spent, shortfall, reasons, and related party CSR dealings.

flow.title: Audit Sequence for Operating Expenses
steps: Obtain expense schedules and conduct monthly trend analysis
Vouch supporting documents (bills, agreements, policies)
Verify business connection and appropriate delegation approval
Calculate prepayments (e.g., insurance) and accruals
Verify Section 135 CSR disclosure details

topics.example: A one-year factory insurance policy paid on 1st October requires 50% to be charged as expense and 50% carried forward as prepaid insurance at 31st March.
remember: Schedule III requires other expenses to be classified under specific heads (Rent, Insurance, Power, Repairs, etc.).
Trading or investment in cryptocurrency/virtual currency requires specific disclosure of holdings and profit/loss.
mistakes: Treating repairs that extend an asset's useful life or capacity as revenue repairs instead of capitalizing them.

quiz.q: Why is an auditor particularly cautious when vouching legal and professional expenses?
o: To negotiate lower legal fees for the client
They may reveal ongoing disputes or unrecorded liabilities
Lawyers are exempt from audit confirmations
Legal fees are always non-deductible for tax
quiz.why: Scrutinizing invoices from legal counsel often alerts the auditor to lawsuits, claims, or regulatory penalties requiring provisions.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a mandatory disclosure regarding CSR under Section 135?
o: Amount required to be spent during the year
Amount of expenditure incurred
Shortfall and reasons for shortfall
Names of all individual beneficiaries of the CSR project
quiz.why: Section 135 disclosures require the amount required, spent, shortfall, nature of activities, and related party transactions, not individual beneficiary names.
